description: DUT ignores Reserved field nonzero values and accepts the TCP packet (RFC 4413 §4.2.3 Reserved)
approach:
[Objective]
Reserved must be ignored on receive — future spec extensions might define some bits. RFC 4413 §4.2.3 makes this explicit. DUT must accept the segment despite the nonzero Reserved.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester ⇄ DUT: handshake.
2. Tester → DUT: data with Reserved bits set.
3. Observation: DUT acks with correct ack_num.

[Pass condition]
DUT acks the data normally.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_handshake_ack / Fail_no_data_ack / Fail_wrong_ack_num — same as HEADER_05

verdicts.Pass: DUT acked data with nonzero Reserved — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_data_ack: No DUT ACK to reserved-nonzero data
verdicts.Fail_wrong_ack_num: DUT ack_num does not acknowledge payload
